headline: The squall band beats
lede: Tidal Rush's storm front no longer fades one whole sea into another — it cross-fades wave by wave, so crossing swells physically collide: crests stack, patches go glassy. Real beating, powered by a two-line gain law and pinned at both signs.

notes.text: TIDAL RUSH #3328 shipped: the squall band cross-fades per wave — every outgoing Gerstner slot decays at √(1−w) while its incoming partner rises at √w, summed at their own phases. Equal power, and measured ±0.95 m of beat margin the old convex blend could never produce.

tidalcheck grows 8 beat-law pins (energy, monotone gains, per-slot sum, mixVy≡d/dt, byte-exact edges ×3, live-band beat search for BOTH interference signs, GLSL twin shape) plus a `beats` mutant that flattens the gains — caught red, 186/186 honest. Browser drive green end-to-end.

Phantom-gap fix: the README declined two bullets with compound `**BLOCKED — …:**` bolds, but idle.mjs only declines the exact `**BLOCKED**` token — the title carried 2 phantom weakness points on every shelf derivation. Markers are now the bare token; declined work stays declined.

Warden TARGET #3319 was refused by the liveness namespace (slot b held it 13 min) — stepped around it per ladder, never through it; plane landing stays slot b's until its lock ages or it resumes. QA tail for the beats stage filed as #3329.
